VISION
To be a leading Real Estate Investment Trust with sustainability and community engagement at the forefront of our 
investment strategies.
MISSION
Creating value for our stakeholders to ensure sustainable 
growth for our KIP REIT community.
• For  our  investors:  We  strive  to  deliver  sustainable  
returns  for  our  investors  with  a  steady  stream  of  
distribution income generated by our unique portfolio 
of assets.
• For  our  business  partners:  We  see  and  treat  our  
tenants  as  our  business  partners.  We  are  building  a  
community of assets as a platform for our business 
partners to expand their enterprises together with our 
growing community of properties, be it local SMEs or 
established brands.
• For  our  shoppers:  We  want  our  shoppers  to  feel  at  
home  at  all  of  our  community-centric  malls,  where  
they  can  access  their  daily  necessities  and  create  
long-lasting  memories  with  other  members  of  their  
communities.
• For  our  employees:  We  treat  all  our  people  with  the  
utmost  respect,  embracing  diversity  and  fostering  
inclusion.  We  are  committed  to  providing  training  
opportunities that empower our employees to reach 
their  full  professional  potential  and  promote  team  
growth.
• For our community: We are committed to helping the 
communities in our areas of operation by supporting 
causes to promote environmental sustainability and 
to foster economic and social development.
We  are  committed  to  leveraging  our  core  capabilities  in

identifying investment opportunities and management of 
our properties to ensure that we maximise value creation 
for  all  of  our  stakeholders.  Our  management  team  takes  
pride  in  making  carefully  considered  decisions  to  deliver  
high-quality investments.
We uphold the highest standards of ethical behavior and 
transparency in all our interactions. Trust and honesty are 
the cornerstones of our relationships with stakeholders.
At  the  heart  of  our  investment  fund  is  our  community,  
with  people  being  central  to  everything  we  do.  We  foster  
a  culture  of  respect,  collaboration,  and  empowerment,  
recognising that our success is built on the diverse talents 
and contributions of our team. We strive to serve each and 
every one of our stakeholders with dedication to maximise 
value.

KIP Real Estate Investment Trust (“KIP REIT”) is a Malaysia domiciled real estate investment trust (“REIT") established 
on  2  November  2016  pursuant  to  the  deed  of  trust  dated  2  November  2016,  an  amended  and  restated  deed  dated  12  
December 2019, and a supplementary deed dated 29 September 2020 (collectively referred to as the “Deeds”) between 
KIP REIT Management Sdn Bhd (“the Manager”) and Pacific Trustees Berhad (“the Trustee”).
KIP REIT was listed on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia Securities Berhad (“Bursa Securities”) on 6 February 2017. As 
such, our conducts are regulated by the Securities Commission Malaysia Act 1993, the Guidelines on Listed Real Estate 
Investment Trusts (“REIT Guidelines”) prescribed by the Securities Commission Malaysia (“SC”), the Main Market Listing 
Requirements  of  Bursa  Securities  (“MMLR”),  the  Rules  of  Bursa  Malaysia  Depository  (“Depository”)  and  taxation  laws  
and rulings.
Subsequent  to  our  unitholders’  approval  on  29  September  2020,  KIP  REIT’s  investment  policy  is  to  invest,  directly  
and  indirectly,  in  a  portfolio  of  income  producing  real  estate  used  primarily  for  retail  purposes,  and  for  industrial  or  
commercial purposes, including, without limiting the generality of the foregoing, warehousing facilities, logistics facilities 
and manufacturing sites as well as real estate-related assets. As at 30 June 2024, KIP REIT’s property portfolio consists 
of eight (8) community-centric malls strategically located in suburban areas across Peninsular Malaysia and three (3) 
industrial properties located at Pulau Indah, Klang, Selangor.

Investment 
Objective
The key objective is to provide unitholders with regular and stable distributions, sustainable 
long-term  unit  price,  distributable  income  and  capital  growth,  while  maintaining  an  
appropriate capital structure.
Investment 
Strategies
The Manager intends to increase the income and consequently, the value of the investment 
properties by implementing the following strategies, including: -
• active asset management and enhancement;

• acquisition growth; and
• capital and risk management.
Authorised 
Investments
Real estate used primarily for retail purposes, and for industrial or commercial purposes, 
including, without limiting the generality of the foregoing, warehousing facilities, logistics 
facilities  and  manufacturing  sites,  special  purpose  vehicles  (“SPVs”),  real-estate  related  
assets, non-real estate-related assets, cash, deposits, money market instruments and any 
other investments not specified above but specified as a permissible investment in the 
REIT Guidelines or as otherwise permitted by the SC.
Authorised 
Investment Limits
The investments of KIP REIT are subject to the following investment limits imposed by the 
REIT Guidelines: -
•  at  least  75.0%  of  KIP  REIT’s  Total  Asset  Value  (“TAV”)  must  be  invested  in  real  estate  
and/or SPVs at all times; and
• not more than 25.0% of KIP REIT’s TAV may be invested in non-real estate-related assets 
and/or cash, deposits and money market instruments, 
provided  that  investments  in  both  real  estate-related  assets  and  non-real  estate-related  
assets are limited as follows: -
• the value of KIP REIT’s investments in securities issued by any single issuer must not 
exceed 5.0% of KIP REIT’s TAV;
•  the  value  of  KIP  REIT’s  investments  in  securities  issued  by  any  group  of  companies  
must not exceed 10.0% of KIP REIT’s TAV; and
• KIP REIT’s investments in any class of securities must not exceed 10.0% of the securities 
issued by any single issuer; or such other limits and investments as may be permitted by 
the SC or the REIT Guidelines.
Borrowing LimitsUp to 50% of the TAV of KIP REIT at the time the borrowings are incurred.
Investors’ ProfileSuitable  for  investors  with  long-term  investment  objectives  who  seeks  regular  income  
distribution and long-term capital appreciation, and who understands the risks related to 
the real estate industry and REITs.
Distribution PolicyAt least 90% of KIP REIT’s distributable income shall be distributed on a quarterly basis.

LETTER TO 
UNITHOLDERS
Dear Valued Unitholders, Dear Valued Unitholders, 
On behalf of the Board of KIP REIT Management 
Sdn  Bhd,  I  am  pleased  to  present  to  you  the  
Annual Report of KIP REIT for the financial 
year ended 30 June 2024 (“FYE 2024”). 
At  KIP  REIT,  our  commitment  to  delivering  
sustainable  value  and  consistent  returns  to  
our  unitholders  has  remained  steadfast.  Our  
strategic  focus  on  the  retail  and  industrial  
property  sectors  in  Malaysia  has  positioned  
us  to  capitalise  on  the  country’s  growing  
consumer  market  and  urbanisation  trends,  
ensuring consistent performance even in the 
challenging market conditions. 
General Economy Overview
Reflecting on the past year, we encountered significant macroeconomic challenges and persistent global volatility arising 
from  post-COVID-19  pandemic,  trade  tensions,  geopolitical  conflicts  and  tightening  monetary  policies.  Despite  these  
hurdles, Malaysia’s economy demonstrated remarkable resilience, with a GDP growth rate of 4.2% in the first quarter of 
2024. This growth was primarily driven by strong domestic demand, improved employment rates and wages, as well as 
increased household spending. In terms of inflation, the rate remained stable at 1.7% in early 2024, compared to 1.6% 
in  2023,  as  a  result  of  moderating  global  commodities  price,  reduced  supply  disruptions,  effective  price  controls  and  
subsidies. 
While  Malaysia  demonstrates  a  recovery  trend,  external  factors  such  as  a  global  economic  slowdown  and  ongoing  
geopolitical tensions may pose risks to fiscal stability and overall growth. Nevertheless, the Malaysian Government 
remains committed to prudent fiscal management and strategic investments through frameworks like Ekonomi MADANI 
and  Budget  2024.  Resilient  domestic  expenditure  and  a  recovering  tourism  sector  are  expected  to  support  continued  
economic growth.
Retail and Industrial Markets Overview
With  the  rise  of  e-commerce  and  technological  advancements  accelerated  by  the  pandemic,  retailers  in  Malaysia  
face numerous challenges. Nonetheless, the sector is navigating these changes effectively. The competitive market is 
driving malls to evolve into experiential centres to attract foot traffic. Despite a cautiously optimistic outlook, economic 
uncertainties  such  as  the  escalating  operational  costs,  may  squeeze  profit  margins  and  drive-up  prices,  affecting 
consumer affordability. However, the Government’s initiatives, such as targeted cash assistance and salary hikes for civil 
servants by the end of 2024 could provide some relief and support to retail activity moving forward.  
 
Datuk Dr Syed Hussain bin Syed Husman, PJN. JP 
Chairman / Senior Independent Non-Executive Director

Retail and Industrial Markets Overview (Cont’d)
In contrast, the industrial sector in Malaysia is flourishing, 
driven by robust e-commerce penetration and consistent 
manufacturing  output.  The  recent  depreciation  of  the  
Malaysian    Ringgit    is    also    expected    to    temporarily    
stimulate  the  foreign  direct  investments.  The  logistics  
industry,  in  particular,  is  benefiting  from  accelerated 
adoption   of   e-commerce   and   experiencing   increased   
demand  for  warehouses  and  distribution  hubs.  Despite  
economic  uncertainties,  the  demand  for  logistics  space  
remains  strong,  supported  by  online  retail  growth  and  a  
positive domestic business climate. Malaysia’s favourable 
business ecosystem and its role as a key supply chain hub 
continue  to  attract  investments,  fostering  growth  in  both  
the logistics and manufacturing sectors.
Business and Financial Highlights
KIP REIT has achieved a higher gross revenue of RM102.16 
million for FYE 2024, representing an increase of RM18.41 
million or 22.0%, as compared to the previous financial 
year.  This  growth  was  attributed  to  the  higher  revenue  
recognised  from  our  three  (3)  industrial  properties  and  
rental  income  derived  from  the  newly  acquired  KIPMall  
Kota  Warisan.  Furthermore,  we  are  glad  to  highlight  that  
our average portfolio occupancy has improved from 92.3% 
as  at  30  June  2023  to  94.1%  as  at  30  June  2024,  mainly  
driven by higher occupancy rate recorded at KIPMall Bangi 
and KIPMall Melaka. 
In  line  with  the  revenue  growth,  we  have  recorded  a  
25.2%  increase  in  net  property  income  for  FYE  2024  as  
compared  to  financial  year  ended  30  June  2023  ("FYE 
2023"). However,  our  profit for  FYE 2024 was recorded 
lower  by  22.2%  due  to  lower  fair  value  gain  recorded  
during the financial year as the fair value in FYE 2023 was 
notably higher due to a remarkable improvement in market 
conditions following the COVID-19 pandemic, which driven 
by  the  gradual  return  to  normalcy  and  recovery  from  the  
Movement Control Order. Nonetheless, our realised profit 
has increased by RM6.77 million or 17.9% from RM37.70 
million  in  FYE  2023  to  RM44.47  million  in  FYE  2024  in  
line  with  the  higher  net  property  income.  As  a  result,  our  
distribution per unit also increased from 6.20 sen for FYE 
2023 to 6.67 sen for FYE 2024.
KIP REIT has also continued to maintain a healthy balance 
sheet  with  a  stronger  portfolio  of  assets  and  healthy  
gearing  ratio  within  the  prescribed  threshold  as  per  the  
REIT Guidelines. 
Further detailed analysis of our financial performance is 
available  in  the  Management  Discussion  and  Analysis  
section of this Annual Report.
Yield-Accretive Acquisition
During  FYE  2024,  we  acquired  KIPMall  Kota  Warisan  for  
a  cash  consideration  of  RM80.00  million.  In  an  effort  to  
maintain  a  healthy  gearing  level,  such  acquisition  was  
funded by a combination of debt and equity financing.

This  acquisition  marks  as  a  valuable  enhancement  to  
our  portfolio  by  bringing  our  total  retail  assets  to  eight  
(8)  malls  and  increasing  our  total  net  lettable  area  by  
approximately  10.7%.  The  strategic  location  of  KIPMall  
Kota  Warisan  also  strengthens  our  industry  position  as  
a geographically well-diversified community-centric mall 
REIT.  In  addition,  we  also  proud  to  highlight  that  KIPMall  
Kota Warisan recorded a high occupancy rate of 99.5% as 
at 30 June 2024. 
Income Distribution 
During the FYE 2024, KIP REIT has made four (4) income 
distributions to the unitholders, totalling RM41.04 million 
or  6.665  sen  per  unit,  representing  90.0%  of  the  current  
year  distributable  income  of  RM45.58  million.  Driven  by  
the  higher  distributable  income  achieved  in  FYE  2024,  
the  distribution  per  unit  has  improved  from  6.20  sen  in  
FYE  2023  to  6.67  sen  per  unit  in  FYE  2024,  translating  
into  a  distribution  yield  of  7.4%  this  year.  These  income  
distributions  are  in  line  with  KIP  REIT’s  objectives  to  
provide stable and attractive returns to our unitholders. 
Asset Enhancement Initiatives (“AEI”)
Proactive asset management is key to unlock the potential 
value  of  our  retail  properties,  enhancing  the  shopping  
experience   and   making   our   malls   more   attractive   to   
both  shoppers  and  retailers.  Therefore,  AEI  are  essential  
to  our  operating  strategies,  ensuring  our  assets  remain  
competitive and valuable in a dynamic real estate market. 
Through  continuous  upgrades,  we  strive  to  meet  the  
evolving  needs  of  our  stakeholders  and  preserve  the  
relevance of our investment properties.
In FYE 2024, we completed the upgrade of mall facilities at 
KIPMall Bangi. The completion of the AEI has significantly 
improved the overall aesthetics of KIPMall Bangi, providing 
a  revitalised  environment  for  retailers  and  an  enhanced  
shopping experience for shoppers. 
We  are  also  undertaking  AEI  work  at  KIPMall  Senawang,  
where we are reconfiguring the retail space by converting 
the  original  fresh  market  into  a  larger  retail  area.  The  
reconfigured  space  will  be  occupied  by  a  new  anchor 
tenant   upon   completion   of   the   AEI,   expected   to   be   
completed by the first quarter of the FYE 2025.

Asset Enhancement Initiatives (“AEI”) (Cont’d)
Other  AEIs  during  FYE  2024  include  the  modenisation  and  improvement  of  sanitary  facilities  across  our  KIPMalls,  as  
well  as  upgrading  works  at  KIPMall  Masai  and  KIPMall  Melaka,  where  we  have  installed  new  exhaust  systems  in  the  
respective food courts.
Looking ahead, we remain committed to continuously evaluating and enhancing our assets through strategic AEIs. By 
doing  so,  we  ensure  our  KIPMalls  remain  competitive  and  attractive,  meeting  the  needs  of  both  our  stakeholders  and  
the communities we serve. This proactive strategy enables us to adapt to market changes, seize new opportunities and 
sustain the long-term value creation of our portfolio.

Sustainable Initiative
At  KIP  REIT,  we  emphasise  integrating  the  Economic,  Environmental,  Social,  and  Governance  (“EESG”)  sustainability  
practices into our operations. With a dedicated Sustainability Working Committee in place, we have continued to advance 
our sustainability journey by implementing various initiatives aligned with 14 United Nations Sustainable Development 
Goals (“UNSDGs”). These initiatives focus on reducing our carbon footprint, optimising energy efficiency and enhancing 
community well-being.  
Throughout the year, we have prioritised the energy consumption at our properties. All KIPMalls are now equipped with 
solar photovoltaic systems to support mall operations. Looking ahead, we aim to increase renewable energy source to 
at least 40.0% by 2030 through upgrading the capacity of solar panels and installing electric vehicle chargers as well as 
acquiring the facility management system across our malls.
In  line  with  our  sustainability  goals,  KIP  REIT  actively  participated  in  the  “Cooler  Earth  Sustainability  Summit  2023”  
and engaged in the “KPMG ESG Talk – Addressing Challenges in Implementing USSB Standards”. These engagements 
have enriched our team’s understanding and commitment to environmental, social and governance practices. We also 
prioritised employee development through various trainings and development programmes, including “Effective Financial 
Budget Control”, “E-Invoicing” and “Agile Leadership”. We believe that nurturing the growth of our people will ultimately 
lead to sustainable business growth in KIP REIT. 
In  demonstrating  our  commitment  to  community  welfare,  we  have  organised  seven  (7)  charitable  events  during  FYE  
2024, focusing on supporting underprivileged families and orphans by distributing essential items. These initiatives have 
positively impacted approximately 6,952 beneficiaries, with a total investment of around RM22,495.80 in community 
projects.
Further  insight  into  our  Sustainability  initiatives  and  commitment  to  mitigating  EESG  risks  is  covered  under  our  
Sustainability Statement of this Annual Report.
Future Outlook
Peering into the future, we anticipate a gradual recovery in the Malaysian economy in 2024, bolstered by robust domestic 
demand and increase in private sector expenditure. Despite the lingering external challenges, headline inflation has been 
relatively well restrained by government subsidies and price controls. Additionally, the Ministry of Finance has forecasted 
an accelerated growth rate of 4.0% to 5.0%, up from 3.7% in 2023.
On  27  May  2024,  the  Trustee  entered  into  a  conditional  Sale  and  Purchase  Agreement  with  DPulze  Ventures  Sdn  Bhd  
for the proposed acquisition of DPulze Shopping Centre, valued at RM320.00 million. Given the prime location of DPulze 
Shopping Centre in Cyberjaya’s primary commercial area, this proposed acquisition is expected to further enhance our 
retail segment portfolio. 
At  KIP  REIT,  we  are  dedicated  to  maintaining  operational  excellence  through  strategic  tenant  management,  effective  
cost control and robust asset enhancement initiatives. Our goal is to scale up our operations and grow our total assets 
under  management  to  RM2.0  billion  over  the  next  three  (3)  years.  By  investing  in  income-producing  real  estate  in  the  
retail and industrial sectors, KIP REIT aims to diversify and expand its portfolio, mitigate risks and capitalise on market 
opportunities. 
Moving forward, we will actively explore potential yield-accretive acquisitions that align with our investment objectives. 
We believe this approach will effectively mitigate risks, increase returns and support sustainable growth in the long run.

We are grateful to have our efforts and achievements recognised by our esteemed media partner, The Edge. In 2023 and

(a) The Edge Malaysia Centurion Club 2023 – Highest Return on Equity over Three Years (REIT category)

Appreciation and Acknowledgement
Reflecting on how we have navigated another challenging year, I would like to take this opportunity to extend my sincere 
appreciation  to  all  our  Board  members  for  their  invaluable  insights,  unwavering  dedication  and  enthusiastic  support.  
Their contributions have been pivotal in shaping the strategic direction of KIP REIT. 
I  would  also  like  to  express  our  heartfelt  gratitude  to  our  unitholders,  the  wider  investment  community,  our  tenants,

shoppers and business partners for placing their trust in us. Your steadfast support and confidence in KIP REIT are 
deeply valued.
As we move forward, we remain focus to delivering value through strategic investments, effective asset management, 
and a steadfast commitment to sustainability. With our dedicated team and clear vision, we are confident that KIP REIT 
will continue to thrive, achieving new heights and delivering attractive returns to our unitholders.
Thank you for your ongoing support.

OVERVIEW OF BUSINESS DIRECTION, OBJECTIVES AND STRATEGIES
KIP REIT was listed on the Main Market of Bursa Securities on 6 February 2017 with the principal investment policy of 
investing in income producing real estate used for retail and for industrial or commercial purposes. It may also invest in 
other investment properties as permissible under the REIT Guidelines or permitted by SC, including real estate related 
assets.  As  at  30  June  2024,  KIP  REIT  has  a  market  capitalisation  of  approximately  RM553.67  million  and  a  portfolio  
independently valued at RM1,061.60 million.
Investment Objective
The key investment objective of KIP REIT is to provide unitholders with regular and stable income distributions as well 
as a sustainable long-term growth in unit price, distribution income and capital growth while maintaining an appropriate 
capital structure.
This is achieved by amongst others, selectively acquiring properties with stable recurring rental income that meets the 
Manager’s investment criteria which are yield accretive or close to yield accretive with the potential for enhancement, 
such that unitholders will be able to enjoy the upside in distribution per unit in the future.
Investment Policy
The principal investment policy of KIP REIT is to invest directly and/or indirectly in a portfolio of income producing real 
estate used primarily for retail purposes, industrial and/or commercial real estate such as but not limited to warehousing 
facilities, logistics facilities and manufacturing sites as well as real estate related assets.
The Manager may, in consultation with the Trustee and subject to the relevant laws and requirements, from time to time 
change the investment policy of KIP REIT. The Trustee shall ensure that it is fully informed at all times by the Manager of 
any changes made by the Manager to the investment policy of KIP REIT. Unless otherwise provided by the relevant laws 
and requirements, any modification to the Deeds involving any material changes to the investment policy set out for KIP 
REIT, must be approved by unitholders by way of a resolution of not less than two-third (2/3) of all unitholders present 
and voting at a unitholders’ meeting duly convened and held in accordance with the Deeds.
Investment Strategies

properties of KIP REIT by adopting the following investment strategies: -

Gross Revenue

Gross revenue mainly comprises the rental income derived from eleven (11) investment properties of KIP REIT. In FYE 2024,

properties  and  rental  income  derived  from  the  newly  acquired  KIPMall  Kota  Warisan.  During  FYE  2024,  approximately  
93.0% of our gross revenue was derived from our retail segment while the remaining 7.0% was derived from our industrial 
segment.
Retail Segment
The retail segment of KIP REIT recorded higher gross revenue in FYE 2024 at RM95.06 million compared to the previous 
financial year at RM80.93 million, mainly due to the higher occupancy rate recorded in most of the investment properties.

recorded during the financial year at 95.3% and 83.9% respectively.

at 97.4% and 96.2% respectively during FYE 2024.

square feet, accounted for 88.5% of the total Net Lettable Area (“NLA”) of 1,204,116 square feet. 
KIP REIT has a long-term master lease agreement with AEON Mall Kinta City for a period of ten (10) years to 2025 with 
an option to renew of five (5) years to 2030, and hence is able to maintain a 100.0% occupancy rate throughout the period 
of  the  master  lease  agreement.  Similarly,  KIP  REIT  also  maintains  a  100.0%  occupancy  rate  for  all  three  (3)  industrial  
properties throughout the 15 years lease agreement signed with the tenants.
KIPMall Tenancy Expiry Profile
KIP REIT is strategically poised with tenancy durations tailored to the tenant's business nature, offering longer tenures 
to key and anchor tenants. This spread across the portfolio efficiently mitigates the risk related to tenant concentration.

As at 30 June 2024, the weighted average lease expiry (“WALE”) is recorded at 1.9 years by Occupied Net Lettable Area 
(“ONLA”), as compared to 2.6 years in FYE 2023. Similarly, by Gross Rental Income (“GRI”), the WALE stands at 1.6 years, 
reflecting downward trend from 2.5 years in FYE 2023. This is mainly due to the major tenancy renewals by KIPMalls in 
FYE 2025 and FYE 2026 following their lease expirations, as shown in the table below. The reduction in WALE aligns with 
KIP  REIT’s  management  strategies  and  business  model.  With  the  shorter  rental  expiry,  we  are  able  to  optimise  rental  
income by adjusting rental rates according to the latest market conditions, ensuring that the lease agreements reflect 
current market trends and demands.
The majority of lease expirations in FYE 2025 are attributed to tenancies in KIPMall Masai and KIPMall Tampoi. However, 
our tenant retention strategy has proven effective in FYE 2024, with a renewal rate of 69.0% for tenants that have reached 
their expiration during the year.

In FYE 2024, KIP REIT has undertaken various AEIs as part of its commitment to delivering sustainable and consistent 
returns to its unitholders. These AEIs amounted to a total investment of RM14.45 million during the financial year which

enhancement at food court, modernisation of fresh market area, roofing system improvement and asphalt paving

their continued relevance in meeting the evolving needs of consumers. Approved AEIs are implemented with the aim of 
providing stable and consistent returns to KIP REIT's unitholders in a sustainable manner.
RISK
The Manager of KIP REIT conducts regular risk management reviews to evaluate significant risks as well as their likelihood 
and potential impact based on the approved risk appetite set by the Board. Appropriate measures are implemented to 
mitigate the likelihood or impact of identified risks.
 
The following section provides a summary of key risks associated with KIP REIT's portfolio: -
Principle RisksMitigating Measures
Economic and Political Landscape
Macroeconomic  trends  and  political  uncertainties  
may result in financial volatility and pose challenges 
in  the  operating  environment  for  KIP  REIT  and  its  
valued business partners.
•  Continuous  monitoring  of  economic  and  political  trends  
to ensure appropriate strategies are adopted in line with 
the business environment.
• Monitoring of occupancy and rental rates and discussions 
with tenants to understand business activities.
Climate Change Risk
Climate change poses a significant risk to both the 
natural environment and human societies worldwide 
that  can  significantly  affect  multiple  sectors, 
ecosystems and populations.
•  Implementation  of  greenhouse  gas  emissions  reduction  
measures  such  as  transitioning  to  renewable  energy  
sources  and  improving  energy  efficiency  to  mitigate 
climate change risks in the long-term.
Credit Control Risk
Inefficiency on rental collections may result in long 
overdue receivables.
•   Operation   department   monitors   the   performance   of

receivables and proactively identifies any potential default 
from outstanding tenants. Weekly updates are presented 
by the Complex Manager (“CM”) and monthly monitoring 
process are conducted during meetings to ensure prompt 
action is taken when necessary.
• Operation department and legal department to discuss on 
the terms of tenancy agreements to gain a comprehensive 
understanding of the rights of the landlord and obligations 
of tenants, including the entitlement for long outstanding 
rental.
•  Standard  notice  will  be  drafted  to  report  long  rental  
outstanding    to    CTOS.    Tenants    which    outstanding    
balances   exceeding   62   days   in   CTOS   portal   will   be   
blacklisted. Verification on such CTOS reporting will be 
done by CM with monthly sign-off and sampling checks 
in place to ensure accuracy and consistency.

GENERAL MARKET OUTLOOK AND MALAYSIA’S ECONOMY
The global economy continues to face challenges arising from the COVID-19 pandemic, deepened geopolitical tensions,

uncertain  trade  policy  and  persistent  tightening  of  monetary  policies.  These  factors  have  increased  the  risk  of  a  
worldwide slowdown. However, according to the World Bank’s Global Economic Prospect report, global economic growth 
is forecasted to stabilise at 2.6% in 2024, with a projected increase to an average of 2.7% in 2025 and 2026, driven mainly 
by the expanding United States economy.
 
In Malaysia, despite escalating global uncertainties and persistent external challenges, the economy remains resilient. 
The Gross Domestic Product (“GDP”) grew to 4.2% in the first quarter of 2024, up from 2.9% in the fourth quarter of 2023. 
This  growth  was  driven  by  strong  domestic  demand,  continuous  improvements  in  employment  and  wages  as  well  as  
rise in household spending. In line with the GDP growth, the Wholesale and Retail Trade sub-sectors continued to show 
strong momentum, supporting its role as a key contributor to the Services sector.

Malaysia inflation remained stable at 1.7% in the first quarter of 2024 
as compared to 1.6% in the preceding quarter, mainly attributed to

related disruptions, existing price controls and provision of subsidies 
for selected items. 
In the second half of 2024, the easing of inflationary pressures and 
recovery  of  the  tourism  industry  are  expected  to  positively  impact  
Malaysia’s  economic  growth.  Private  sector  expenditure  is  also  
anticipated to remain as the main driver of our economic activities, 
supported  by  stronger  domestic  demand.  Government’s  initiatives  
such as rationalisation of subsidies, targeted cash assistance and 
the  growing  trend  of  social  commerce  are  also  expected  to  boost  
private consumption. 
 
In  addition  to  these  initiatives,  the  Malaysian  Government  has  also  implemented  various  measures,  such  as  Ekonomi  
MADANI  framework,  the  Twelfth  Malaysia  Plan  and  Budget  2024  to  propel  Malaysia  towards  a  more  robust  growth  
trajectory. These strategies and programmes, coupled with the nation’s strong economic fundamentals, are expected to 
support the momentum of the economy to grow within the estimated range of 4% to 5% in 2024. 
RETAIL MARKET OVERVIEW 
In an era of rapid transformation and rising consumer expectations, the global retail landscape is undergoing significant 
changes, redefining the way businesses engage with consumers. The surge of e-commerce, integration of technology 
and experiential retail are driving rapid evolution within the retail sector. 
Malaysia’s  retail  sector  is  closely  aligning  itself  with  these  global  transformations,  having  experienced  in  navigating

challenges such as the pandemic, embracing digital advancements and adapted to ever-changing consumer behaviour. 
Shopping  has  transcended  its  traditional  form;  it  no  longer  just  about  making  purchases,  but  also  creating  immersive  
experiences for consumers. Malls are evolving into experiential centres, integrating entertainment and leisure components 
to attract sustained footfall amid the pressures of e-commerce.

However, the retail sector faces significant challenges, including the rising cost of living and the increase in the service 
tax rate from 6.0% to 8.0%, both of which are expected to impact consumer spending. Additionally, escalating operational 
costs such as rent, utilities and labour cost, are likely to squeeze the profit margins for retailers, particularly small 
businesses. This may potentially lead to an increase in product prices, affecting consumer affordability. 
Despite  these  challenges,  Retail  Group  Malaysia  forecasts  a  4.0%  growth  rate  for  the  retail  industry  for  the  year  2024,  
indicating  the  sector’s  resilience  and  its  ability  to  adapt  the  ever-changing  consumer  demands  and  expectations.  
Furthermore, with the Government’s announcement of a salary hike for civil servants by the end of 2024, along with the 
newly  introduced  Akaun  Fleksibel  (Account  3)  by  the  Employees  Provident  Fund  which  offers  flexible  withdrawals  for  
meeting short-term financial needs, are anticipated to further stimulate retail activity and potentially bolster the retail 
market. 
INDUSTRIAL MARKET OVERVIEW
The  industrial  sector  in  Malaysia  continues  to  thrive,  underpinned  by  robust  investment  volume,  strong  e-commerce  
integration and consistent manufacturing output. 
The rapid expansion of e-commerce has contributed immensely to the logistics industry, leading to increased demand 
for properties like warehouses, distribution hubs and logistics facilities. Despite the prevailing economic uncertainties, 
the demand for logistics space is expected to remain strong, mainly supported by ongoing growth of online retail, shifting 
consumer  behaviours  and  a  positive  domestic  business  environment.  Furthermore,  the  recent  depreciation  of  the  
Malaysian Ringgit is anticipated to temporarily boost the foreign direct investments.
In 2023, Malaysia recorded a 14.9% increase in the total value of industrial property transactions, reaching RM12.24 billion 
in 2023 as compared to RM10.65 billion in 2022. This highlights Malaysia’s attractiveness as an investment destination 
due to its favourable business ecosystem and strategic role as a key supply chain hub.

PROSPECTS
As we progress through 2024, the Malaysian economy is poised for steady growth, driven by strong domestic demand 
and  anticipated  acceleration  in  GDP  growth.  Despite  ongoing  external  challenges,  supportive  policy  actions  by  the  
Government, such as the Ekonomi MADANI framework, reflect a commitment to enhancing economic resilience and are 
expected to bolster Malaysia’s short to medium-term economic growth prospects.
On  27  May  2024,  KIP  REIT  announced  that  the  Trustee  had  entered  into  a  conditional  SPA  with  DPulze  Ventures  for  
the  proposed  acquisition  of  DPulze  Shopping  Centre  for  a  purchase  consideration  of  RM320.0  million.  This  proposed  
acquisition strategically aligns with KIP REIT’s investment objectives, aimed at enhancing our retail segment portfolio 
and providing stable income distributions.
KIP REIT maintain a positive outlook, buoyed by the strong performance of our existing property portfolio and strategic 
initiatives to enhance leasing and operational efficiencies. Our AEI, coupled with strategic investments in high-quality 
assets, are integral to our growth strategy. Over the next three (3) years, we aim to scale up our asset base to RM2.00 
billion. We will continue to identify and evaluate potential growth opportunities in income-producing real estate across 
retail  and  industrial  sectors,  including  industrial  facilities,  logistic  facilities  and  warehouses,  to  capitalise  on  market  
opportunities and drive sustainable growth.

INVESTOR RELATIONS AND 
CORPORATE COMMUNICATIONS
At  KIP  REIT,  the  Manager  truly  believes  that  open  and  transparent  communication  is  the  cornerstone  of  a  successful  
connection between KIP REIT and our various stakeholders to build trust, values and confidence in the long run. We 
recognise that timely and accurate information enables our stakeholders to gain meaningful insights and make informed 
decisions which align to their interests and objectives. 
The  Manager  has  established  a  corporate  communication  framework  that  outlines  the  engagement  approach  and  
frequency for each group of stakeholders, catering to the different levels of engagement and information required. It is 
also reviewed annually by the Board to review the effectiveness of communication channels adopted by the Manager. 
Through the dedicated efforts made to engage with the stakeholders via various communication channels as shown in 
the following sections, the Manager is able to gain a better understanding of the stakeholders’ expectations. 
Press Release and Media Coverage 
As  part  of  our  on-going  efforts  to  promote  timely  and  transparent  communication  with  the  investment  community  as  
well  as  to  build  strong  relationships  with  the  stakeholders,  the  Manager  has  continuously  interacted  actively  with  our  
investment community through press release. This approach serves as a valuable platform for us to provide the public 
with an in-depth understanding on our business development, trend, challenges and prospects. 
During the financial year under review, the Manager, through the Investor Relations (“IR”) Team, announced the following

press releases on Bursa Securities to share its financial performance and milestones achieved over the period: - 
DateTitle
24 July 2023KIP REIT Finishes FY2023 on a Strong Note
4 October 2023KIP REIT Unitholders Approve Acquisition of KIPMall Kota Warisan
20 October 2023KIP REIT Reports 18.2% Increase in Realised Profit After Tax for Q12024
29 January 2024KIP REIT’s Growth Trajectory Surges Further, Records Best Second Quarter Earnings Ever
5 March 2024KIP REIT Unveils New Logo, Embracing Growth and Sustainability Initiatives
23 April 2024KIP REIT’s 9MFY2024 PAT Surges 13.9% to RM31.3 Million
On top of those press releases announced on Bursa Securities, we have also leveraged on a broader media exposure via 
newspaper publications, such as News Straits Times, Sin Chew Daily, The Edge, The Star, The Sun, eNanyang, Business 
Today,  Berita  Harian,  Berita  Kini  and  Dagang  News,  in  which  these  news  are  accessible  on  our  company’s  website  at  
https://www.kipreit.com.my/newsroom/. 
Equity Research via Bursa Research Incentive Scheme (“Bursa RISE”)
KIP REIT is one of the first batch of participating listed companies in Bursa RISE programme, which aims to improve the 
visibility of listed companies and their trading activity through research coverage and marketing activities by engaging 
the licensed research analysts.
Throughout the financial year under review, our regular engagement with Affin Hwang Investment Bank Berhad (“Affin 
Hwang Investment”) and TA Securities Holdings Berhad (“TA Securities”) in the quarterly financial results briefings 
ensured timely dissemination of financial and operational updates during the quarterly results announcements. The 
IR Team, together with the Manager, also updated the KIP REIT’s corporate factsheet, portfolio updates, prospects and 
outlook as well as the Environmental, Social and Governance (“ESG”) initiatives on a quarterly basis at the Analyst and 
Fund  Manager  Meeting  Day  after  the  quarterly  results  announcements.  In  addition,  we  also  organised  one-on-one  
meetings with other analysts and fund managers which allow for focused discussions.

In FYE 2024, KIP REIT had convened both the Seventh AGM and Unitholders’ Meeting virtually on 4 October 2023. 
The AGM is the principal forum for dialogue with unitholders. The Board is dedicated to engage in constructive dialogue 
with our unitholders and providing the necessary information or clarification to address any of their queries. Through the 
AGM, the Board is able to update the unitholders on KIP REIT’s strategic development as well as any portfolio updates, 
and  simultaneously,  the  unitholders  are  able  to  gain  a  better  and  deeper  understanding  on  our  business  strategies,  
performance,  and  future  prospects.  Unitholders  are  also  encouraged  to  exercise  their  voting  rights  during  the  AGM  to  
ensure that their voices are heard, and their collective interests are represented. From FYE 2021 onwards, the Manager 
has held fully virtual AGM through live streaming and online voting via Remote Participation Electronic Voting (“RPEV”) 
facilities to enhance the accessibility and convenience for our unitholders.
Whilst KIP REIT conducts AGM every year, the Manager may call for Unitholders’ Meeting for any specific situations that 
require  the  attention  and  approval  of  unitholders  beyond  the  AGM.  The  Unitholders’  Meeting  held  on  4  October  2023  
was mainly to obtain unitholders’ approval on the proposed acquisition of KIPMall Kota Warisan and proposed private 
placement. Unitholders were also allowed to raise their queries or concerns and exercise their voting rights during the 
Unitholders’ Meeting.

ensures  that  the  notice  of  AGM  is  circulated  to  unitholders  at  least  28  days  prior  to  the  AGM.  We  also  advertised  our  
notice  of  AGM  in  one  (1)  nationally  circulated  daily  newspapers  for  a  wider  public  outreach.  The  Manager  believes

CORPORATE GOVERNANCE 
OVERVIEW STATEMENT
The Board acknowledges the importance of adopting good corporate governance in KIP REIT as a fundamental part of 
discharging its duties to protect and enhance unitholders’ value and stakeholders’ interest. The Board is fully committed to 
maintaining effective corporate governance practices as recommended in the Malaysian Code on Corporate Governance 
(“MCCG”). 
As  part  of  this  commitment,  the  Board  is  pleased  to  present  this  Corporate  Governance  Overview  Statement  (“CG  
Statement”), which provides a concise overview of the application of the following three (3) key corporate governance 
principles set out in the MCCG throughout the Group during FYE 2024:- 
Principle A - Board Leadership and Effectiveness;
Principle B - Effective Audit and Risk Management; and
Principle C - Integrity in Corporate Reporting and Meaningful Relationship with Stakeholders.
This  CG  Statement  is  prepared  pursuant  to  Paragraph  15.25(1)  of  the  MMLR  of  Bursa  Securities  with  guidance  from  
Practice Note 9 of the MMLR of Bursa Securities.
The Manager
KIP  REIT  is  constituted  by  the  Deeds  entered  into  between  the  Manager  and  the  Trustee.  In  accordance  with  these  
Deeds, the Manager is entrusted to manage KIP REIT with due care and diligence to safeguard the best interests of the 
unitholders. The Manager holds a valid Capital Markets Services License (“CMSL”) licensed by the Securities Commission 
Malaysia (“SC”) to perform such management activities. The Trustee, on the other hand, is tasked with the responsibility 
to oversee such management on behalf of unitholders.

•  Cultivating Ethical Practices
•  Transforming into Low Carbon Assets
•  Nurturing Talent and Community Engagement

and priorities. These engagements enable KIP REIT’s to have better understanding on the needs and expectations 
of stakeholders, thereby improving its sustainability.

environment, the Board has incorporated sustainability-related criteria into the Board evaluation for FYE 2024.

The Board is pleased to present this Statement on Risk Management and Internal Control (“Statement”), which outlines 
the  main  features  of  risk  management  and  internal  control  system  in  KIP  REIT  for  the  FYE  2024.  This  Statement  is  
prepared pursuant to Paragraph 15.26(b) of MMLR and Principle B of MCCG, with guidance from the Statement on Risk 
Management and Internal Control: Guidelines for Directors of Listed Issuers issued by Bursa Securities. 
BOARD RESPONSIBILITIES
The  Board  assumes  the  ultimate  responsibility  over  KIP  REIT’s  overall  risk  management  and  internal  control  system.  
Guided  by  the  Board  Charter,  it  is  responsible  to  review  the  adequacy  of  KIP  REIT’s  internal  control  framework  and  to  
ensure that all identified risks are properly managed in order to safeguard our assets, unitholders’ investments and 
various stakeholders’ interests. In this regard, the Board has in place an ongoing review and assessment on KIP REIT’s

risk management and internal control system with appropriate risk appetite in this evolving business environment.
Whilst  the  Board  takes  the  oversight  responsibility  over  KIP  REIT’s  risk  management  and  internal  control  system,  it  is  
supported by the ARMC to oversee and monitor the said system on an on-going basis. 
In  view  of  the  inherent  limitation  in  any  risk  management  and  internal  control  system,  KIP  REIT’s  risk  management  and  
internal control system is designed to identify and manage risks within an acceptable level, rather than eliminate them. Thus, 
it can only provide reasonable but not absolute assurance of its effectiveness against any material financial misstatement, 
loss, fraud or any unforeseeable events. Nonetheless, the Board, together with the ARMC, is committed to cultivate a sound 
and resilient culture by maintaining a robust risk management and internal control system within KIP REIT.
MAIN FEATURES OF RISK MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Risk management plays a pivotal role in today’s dynamic business landscape. In this regard, the Board has adopted a 
robust Enterprise Risk Management (“ERM”) system in accordance with ISO 31000:2018, an international risk management 
framework  that  provides  a  set  of  risk  management  guidelines  and  principles  from  the  International  Organisation  for  
Standardisation (“ISO”). 
KIP REIT’s Directors and employees are guided by the ERM Standard Operating Manual for the detailed description and 
procedures of the ERM system. All the risk identified by the ARMC are documented in the Risk Register to facilitate the 
on-going review with proper mitigation plans to manage the risks to an acceptable level.

Both the ERM framework and process are closely associated and interrelated, of which the ERM framework outlines the 
method adopted by KIP REIT for the integration of ERM within the organisation whereas the ERM process illustrates the 
overall risk management procedures.
As viewed from the ERM framework, KIP REIT’s ERM system is established on the foundation of six (6) key components. 
Fundamentally,  the  ERM  system  relies  on  the  leadership  direction  and  decision-making  from  the  Board  and  Senior  
Management.  In  this  regard,  the  Board  is  responsible  for  setting  KIP  REIT’s  risk  appetite  and  risk  tolerance  level  by

aligning  with  its  risk  management  objectives.  In  addition,  the  Board  shall  instil  the  Management’s  accountability  and  
oversight in the integration of ERM system to ensure its efficiency and effectiveness. 
Meanwhile, the remaining four (4) components, i.e. design, implementation, evaluation and improvement, refer to the key 
elements and procedures in the ERM system to ensure its relevance to KIP REIT’s business nature as well as the industry 
that it operates in.
With  the  adoption  of  ERM  framework,  the  Board  has  developed  a  six-step  ERM  process,  covering  from  establishing  
the context to communication and consultation. At first, the Board together with the ARMC shall establish a common 
understanding on the basis in which the risk management activities operate in. In this phase, the Board and ARMC shall 
consider both KIP REIT’s internal and external environment in order to determine the strategic and organisational context, 
risk management context, risk evaluation criteria and stakeholder identification.
Subsequently,  the  Board  and  the  ARMC  undertakes  a  set  of  risk  control  self-assessment  process  within  the  context  
established earlier. All the potential and current risks related to KIP REIT are firstly identified and documented in the Risk 
Register and subsequently analysed by their likelihood and impact by aligning the existing control within KIP REIT. Such 
result is then documented in the Risk Heat Map, Risk Register and Corporate Risk Profile.
 
In the event if the Board and ARMC think that existing control is inadequate, they will develop the appropriate risk treatment 
strategy to address the identified risks, which include risk avoidance, risk reduction, risk sharing and risk acceptance. 
In this process, the Board and ARMC will perform a cost-benefit analysis for selecting the most suitable risk treatment 
approach to ensure that it brings the expected protection/impact within the desired risk tolerance level.
The Board and ARMC review the Risk Register on a quarterly basis to ensure that the risks identified are current and 
relevant to the latest business environment and that the risk responses are effective to address the relevant risks within 
the acceptable risk tolerance level. In this regard, all Head of Departments are required to maintain risk records within 
their purview and perform regular reporting to the Legal and Compliance Manager, who will in turn report to the ARMC.
Last  but  not  least,  the  Board  and  ARMC  shall  ensure  that  communication  and  consultation  are  present  continuously  
throughout  the  course  of  the  ERM  system.  This  shall  allow  all  stakeholders  to  attain  a  common  understanding  on  
KIP  REIT’s  risk  management  system  as  well  as  its  overall  risk  appetite.  Where  necessary,  risk  related  trainings  will  be  
organised to enhance our employees’ risk management knowledge and awareness.

In order to ensure the effectiveness of ERM, the Board has in place a comprehensive ERM governance structure to monitor 
the implementation of ERM system within the organisation. Whilst the Board is supported by the External Auditors and 
governed by the local regulator, it has also established three (3) lines of defence as shown in the figure above. 
The first (1st) line of defence, which is also known as operational management, refers to the controls in place at operational 
levels where each department/function is responsible to own and manage their respective risks within their purview. 
For the second (2nd) line of defence, the risk management department/function is tasked to monitor risk management 
practices and performance within the organisation. They are also empowered to facilitate the top-down communication 
of risk information to relevant stakeholders. The Risk Management Working Group, led by CEO, will periodically review 
the Risk Register and to update the ARMC at the scheduled meetings in the event if there is any emerging risk identified. 
 
The  internal  audit  function  serves  as  our  third  (3rd)  line  of  defence  where  it  provides  independent  assurance  on  the  
effectiveness of KIP REIT’s governance as well as risk management and internal control system which are supported by 
our 1st and 2nd lines of defence. Internal audit is essential in governing the ERM system as it evaluates and examines 
the existing controls to identify any internal control deficiencies which require further improvement and enhancement.
Both  the  Senior  Management  and  ARMC  are  serving  as  the  governing  bodies  to  oversee  KIP  REIT’s  risk  management  
activities. Where Senior Management is entrusted to monitor all three (3) lines of defences while the ARMC is authorised 
to oversee the internal audit function directly. The ARMC shall also review the adequacy of KIP REIT’s risk appetite and 
tolerance level annually. The Board, who is the highest governing body, remains committed to reviewing KIP REIT’s risk 
management system regularly or as and when necessary.

KIP REIT firmly believes in governance rooted in integrity and ethics. We see this as a crucial foundation for incorporating 
sustainability  goals  and  objectives  into  our  decision-making,  enhancing  transparency,  managing  risks,  and  ensuring  
long-term success.
Effective  ESG  management  requires  strong  leadership  to  ensure  that  day-to-day  operations  and  business  decisions  
aligned with KIP REIT’s vision and sustainability goals. This approach helps build trust and confidence across all 
stakeholder groups. 
To  strengthen  our  approach  and  efficiently  manage  sustainability  initiatives,  we  have  implemented  a  three-tier 
sustainability governance structure. The Manager’s Board of Directors (“Board”) sits at the apex of this structure, 
providing overall guidance for KIP REIT’s sustainability direction. Supporting the Board is the Sustainability Working 
Committee  ("Committee"),  headed  by  the  Chief  Sustainability  Officer  (“CSO”).  This  Committee  is  responsible  for 
implementing sustainability strategies, managing material sustainability matters, and developing relevant policies and 
targets. Furthermore, the Sustainability Working Committee, in collaboration with the CSO and the Legal Manager, will 
hold quarterly committee meetings to address ESG-related matters.

SUSTAINABILITY POLICY
 
KIP REIT’s Sustainability Policy (“Policy”), rooted in our ESG Framework, outlines our commitment to cultivating a resilient,

high-performing corporate culture and guides our ESG strategy. This Policy forms the foundation of our ESG commitments 
towards long-term growth and helps integrate sustainable practices across our operations and value chain. The Board 
has reviewed and approved this Policy , which undergoes periodic assessments to maintain its continued relevance and 
applicability.
The Policy’s key objectives are:
►	Establish and monitor crucial ESG and economic indicators: These indicators reflect our environmental, social, and 
governance responsibilities and economic performance.
►	Achieve long-term business sustainability: We aim to weave sustainability into our operation fabric while addressing 
stakeholder concerns.
►	Implement sustainable business practices: Our goal is to positively impact the local economy, protect natural 
resources, and benefit the local community.
Commitments have been established by the Company for the respective ESG matters: 
 
GOVERNANCE
KIP  REIT  is  dedicated  to  upholding  high  standards  of  corporate  governance  and  adhering  to  
ethical business practices to protect stakeholder values and interests. We also comply with 
applicable laws and regulations to minimize risks in data protection and cybersecurity.
ECONOMIC
We aim to generate value for our stakeholders through stable and regular income distribution and 
capital appreciation. KIP REIT is committed to providing adequate work, productive employment, 
and platforms for SMEs to expand their businesses within the local community.
SOCIAL
KIP  REIT  works  to  create  a  safe,  healthy,  diverse,  and  inclusive  work  environment  with  fair  
opportunities for all workers. We adhere to strict labour regulations, prioritize product quality 
and customer satisfaction, and conduct supplier assessments to ensure suppliers address the 
pertinent social criteria. We safeguard tenants through security and crime prevention strategies, 
and have an emergency response plan in place.
ENVIRONMENT
To  reduce  our  carbon  footprint  and  other  environmental  impacts,  KIP  REIT  is  focused  on  
implementing responsible resource management. We strive to assess and control GHG emissions 
arising from our business operations and promote the use of energy-efficient technology and 
renewable energy generation at our properties where practical.

Materiality Assessment Process
Step 1: Review on the Stakeholder Group and Material Sustainability Matters Identified
We conduct a comprehensive materiality assessment every two years to prioritise sustainability issues based on their 
economic, environmental, social, and governance impacts on our operations. 
In FY2024, we undertook a thorough review of our stakeholder groups and sustainability matters. This process ensured 
ongoing relevance to our business strategy, operations, and current market trends, while aligning with the sustainability 
reporting frameworks. Our assessment confirmed that all fifteen (15) of our existing material matters continue to align 
with KIP REIT’s strategic priorities and stakeholder expectations.
We periodically update our assessment to maintain its accuracy, relevance and reflectiveness of our evolving business 
landscape. This iterative process enables us to align our strategy with day-to-day operation, address business needs 
and create long-term sustainable value for our stakeholders. This year’s internal assessment reaffirmed the continued 
relevance of our fifteen (15) material matters to both our businesses and stakeholders. 
Looking ahead, we are committed to conducting a more extensive materiality assessment, engaging directly with key 
stakeholders to gather their insights, and publishing the results of this comprehensive evaluation in our next Statement. 
By maintaining this rigorous approach to materiality, we ensure that our sustainability efforts remain focused, impactful, 
and aligned with the expectations of our diverse stakeholder base.
Step 2: Review on the Prioritized Sustainability Matters
We reevaluated the prioritisation outcomes of sustainability matters from FY2023. The material topics were ranked 
according to their importance and potential impact on KIP REIT and its stakeholders, using survey methods that collected 
inputs from both external and internal stakeholders. 
These surveys measured how crucial each topic was to KIP REIT and its stakeholders. Our review confirmed that 
the  ranking  of  sustainability  matters  remains  consistent  with  KIP  REIT’s  strategies  and  plans  and  what  stakeholders  
anticipate.

maintaining financial health and achieving sustainable success.

management if needed.

media anytime.
Through active engagement with tenants, KIP REIT can identify areas for improvement and implement changes that 
enhance tenant experience and satisfaction. 
This proactive approach not only addresses immediate concerns but also fosters a collaborative atmosphere where

Maintaining a robust commitment to ethical standards and legal compliance, KIP REIT recognizes that upholding strong 
governance and integrity is crucial to our long-term success and trust with stakeholders. We particularly emphasize

At KIP REIT, we are steadfast in our commitment to ethical standards and legal compliance. Recognizing the critical 
importance of governance and integrity to our long-term success. Our dedication is reflected in several key policies and 
practices aimed at fostering a transparent and responsible corporate environment.
 
 The Board Charter
The Board Charter is founded on the principles and best practices of the Malaysian Code on Corporate Governance 
(“MCCG”), serves as the cornerstone of our governance framework. It outlines the roles, responsibilities, and expected 
professional conduct of our Board members. 
 Anti-Bribery Management System (“ABMS”)
Our  Compliance  Department  is  responsible  for  the  design,  implementation,  and  management  of  the  Anti-Bribery 
Management System (“ABMS”). The ABMS is KIP REIT’s systematic approach to managing corruption risks and includes 
comprehensive practices such as:
• Leadership and commitments from the Senior Management 
• Corruption risk assessment
•    Compliance with Anti-Bribery and Corruption (“ABC”) Policy 
• Maintaining of Whistleblowing Policy 
• Management procedures on Conflict of Interest 
• Due diligence check for risk areas 
• Communication, awareness and training on anti-corruption 
• Monitoring, reporting and investigating on whistleblowing and corruption cases
The Compliance Officer plays a crucial role in this process by providing guidance on bribery and corruption issues, 
monitoring and evaluating the ABMS’s performance, and reporting on its effectiveness to the Audit and Risk Management 
Committee (“ARMC”).
 The Anti-Bribery and Corruption Policy (“ABC Policy”) 
This  Policy  prohibits  employees  and  Directors  from  receiving  or  soliciting  gifts  and  hospitality  from  third  parties. 
Donations and sponsorships are permitted only with prior approval from KIP REIT. Additionally, the Policy bans facilitation

payments and mandates due diligence on major service providers and business associates, ensuring they adhere to our 
anti-bribery standards.
Moving forward, the Manager aims to review the ABC Policy to ensure it aligns with the latest 
MCCG requirements and to verify its continued effectiveness.

 Conflict of Interest Policy
In KIP REIT, conflict of interest might arise where a person’s ability to perform his/her duties effectively and impartially 
is potentially impaired by the personal interests, considerations or relationships. 
KIP REIT’s Conflict of Interest Policy requires all Directors and employees to avoid situations that could impair their 
ability to perform duties impartially. Any potential conflicts must be declared immediately to maintain transparency 
and integrity within our operations.
 
Supplier and Business Partner Assessment
Before establishing any business relationship, the Manager conducts thorough due diligence on all service providers and 
business associates. This process involves the completion of a Pre-Qualified Supplier Form by the Management, which 
is a result of the due diligence activity.
The due diligence process includes several key steps:
• Identification and Verification: Confirming the background of service providers.
• Risk Assessment: Evaluating their potential risks included risks related to bribery and corruption.
This comprehensive evaluation ensures that all partners align with KIP REIT’s standards for integrity and compliance.
 
Code of Conduct and Code of Ethics
KIP  REIT’s  Code  of  Conduct  for  the  Board  of  Directors  establishes  an  ethical  framework  that  promotes  prudent  
and professional behaviour. It mandates Directors to avoid conflicts of interest, refrain from accepting extravagant 
gifts or engaging in bribery, fraud, money laundering, insider trading, and to maintain confidentiality in all Board 
deliberations and communications.
Similarly,  our  Code  of  Conduct  for Employees  encapsulates  our  core  ethical  values  and  commitment  to  integrity,  
transparency, and professionalism. Employees are expected to uphold these standards consistently in all business 
dealings, contributing to the Company’s social and environmental growth.
KIP REIT’s Code of Ethics for Employees further reinforces these principles by addressing specific topics, including:
•   Acting in alignment with the Company’s interests.
•   Avoiding conflicts of interest.
•   Adhering to a strict no-gift policy.
•   Upholding zero tolerance for bribery, fraud, and money laundering.
•   Ensuring confidentiality in management information and communication.
•   Complying with all legal requirements.
These codes collectively guide our Directors and employees in maintaining the highest standards of ethical conduct, 
fostering a culture of integrity and responsibility within KIP REIT.

In the realm of modern businesses, digital services are now ubiquitous, making data privacy and cybersecurity essential 
for long-term viability. As a REIT, safeguarding customer and tenant data from cybersecurity threats is a top priority for 
us. 
 
 Protecting Digital Assets and Ensuring IT Security
At KIP REIT, safeguarding our digital assets and adhering to the Personal Data Protection Act (“PDPA”) is paramount. 
To  achieve  this,  we  have  implemented  an  Information  Technology  Security  Policy  (“ITSP”)  designed  to  protect  
sensitive data and defend against potential security threats and breaches.
The use of IT resources for any illegal activities or purposes beyond those expressly permitted by the Company is 
strictly prohibited. This ensures that all digital operations remain secure and compliant with our policies.
 External IT Support and Maintenance 
To enhance the security and functionality of our IT systems, we engage external vendors to provide comprehensive 
support and maintenance. These vendors are tasked with:

Understanding and assessing KIP REIT’s existing IT infrastructure.

Performing  monthly  routine  checks  to  update  and  maintain  our  server  and  network  equipment,  including  
database servers, backup servers, firewalls, and disaster recovery servers.

Assisting KIP REIT in troubleshooting and resolving server and system issues related to data backup.

Ensuring compliance with cybersecurity standards.

Assisting in Business Continuity Plan (“BCP”) testing to ensure our operations can withstand and recover from 
disruptions.
To  further  bolster  our  defences  against  cybersecurity  attacks,  we  conducted  a  BCP  testing 
in  May  2024.  This  included  a  Disaster  Recovery  Plan  (“DRP”)  exercise,  which  simulated

KIP REIT is committed to contributing to the shift towards a low carbon economy, recognizing the heightened interest

the regulatory requirements of Bursa Malaysia’s Main Market Listing Requirements this year. This proactive step aims 
to position KIP REIT for long-term success and climate resilience amidst a rapidly changing business environment. We 
are focused on managing climate-related risks and seizing opportunities that could impact our business, strategy, and 
financial planning.
Climate change poses significant challenges to Malaysia, affecting its environment, economy, and society on multiple 
fronts. The Climate Risk Country Profile: Malaysia (2021) by the World Bank Group and Asian Development Bank paints 
a concerning picture, projecting a potential temperature increase of 2.0°C by the 2050s under a worst-case scenario. 
Malaysia is already grappling with the consequences of increased extreme weather events. For instance, the 2023 Nature 
Disaster Report from Agensi Pengurusan Bencana Malaysia (“NADMA”) highlighted widespread flooding across Malaysia, 
resulting in casualties and displacing thousands of families.
Amid  global  concerns  voiced  by  environmentalists  and  activists,  the  looming  threats  of  heatwaves,  rising  sea  levels,  
floods, hurricanes, droughts, and heavy rainfall underscore the urgent need for action on climate change. These risks 
include biodiversity loss, water scarcity, heightened health risks, displacement, and economic disruption. Such potential 
disasters could unfold if global temperatures surpass 1.5°C above preindustrial levels.
Our  strategies  to  address  climate-related  risks  and  ensure  water  security  in-clude  setting  emission  reduction 
targets, implementing standardized water management procedures and engaging stakeholders. KIP REIT future plan 
is to incorporate a carbon emission price to embed the costs into our business decisions. This approach guides our 
investments, encourages emission reduction efforts, and supports our carbon reduction targets.

Water Security
Although Malaysia generally experiences low water risk and most of our properties are located in non-water-stressed 
areas, we have encountered frequent unplanned interruptions in municipal water supply. 
Water security is critical for KIP REIT due to our water-intensive operations, particularly in food and beverage outlets, 
cooling towers, toilets, pantries, water features, irrigation, and washing. Through proactive and sustainable measures, we 
have ensured a consistent water supply to support our business operations. 
Below are the future strategies and initiatives aimed at enhancing our water security:
•    Installation of Water-efficient Fixtures: Implementation of water-saving fittings such as self-closing taps and 
waterless urinals to minimize water wastage.
•    Diversification of Water Sources: Reducing reliance on a single water supply by diversifying our water sources.
•    Development of Water Crisis Standard Operating Procedure ("SOP"): Establishment of an emergency response plan 
for water disruptions, including:
•    Adjusting the operation of toilets and shutting down pressure pumps to reduce flush volume.
•    Decreasing air-conditioning usage and raising mall temperatures to lower cooling tower water consumption.
•    Rescheduling activities that require significant water usage, such as servicing air-conditioning equipment.
These measures are designed to enhance our resilience to water-related challenges and ensure sustainable management 
of water resources across our operations.

Based on the climate Value at Risk (“VaR”) analysis under +4.0°C global warming scenario, KIP REIT property portfolio 
shows an overall low VaR, despite being vulnerable to risks such as flash floods and water seepage during heavy rainfall. 
Specifically, two properties exhibit low VaR, while four have medium VaR. Three properties KIPMall Masai, KIPMall Kota 
Tinggi, and KIPMall Tampoi are classified as high VaR due to their proximity to the coastline. Nevertheless, KIP REIT will 
improve  and  implement  mitigation  measures  to  enhance  these  properties’  resilience  against  the  worst-case  climate  
change scenarios.
Moving forward, KIP REIT will continue to vigilantly monitor all properties to safeguard against significant climate-related 
physical risks such as floods, intensified rainfall, and landslides. Appropriate mitigation strategies will be deployed as 
needed to ensure the ongoing protection and resilience of our portfolio.
Risk Assessment Water Source
Access to high quality freshwater, requiring minimal treatment, is crucial for our operations. We depend on municipal 
water supply and treatment facilities, which are contingent on the availability of freshwater. Any contamination could 
disrupt our withdrawal and supply operations, potentially impacting our business activities. Conversely, we are obligated 
to ensure that the water discharged from our properties meets permissible standards.
Flooding poses a significant threat to KIP REIT assets, potentially causing extensive damage and significant repair costs. 
Temporary evacuation or unavailability of spaces for tenants could lead to income loss during repairs. Costs associated 
with business interruption, insurance claims, temporary relocations, and supporting tenants in resuming operations may 
also arise.
Water Risk Analysis
KIP REIT used the Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas developed by Water Risk Atlas (“WRI”) to assess and visualize water-
related risks across our properties. Although our properties in Malaysia face exposure to risks such as flash floods and 
water seepage, they are generally located in urban areas that are not considered water stressed. The WRI has assessed 
Malaysia as having a low to medium overall water risk.

We channel 100% of the wastewater from KIP REIT properties into the municipal sewerage system managed by Indah

GREEN BUILDING COMMITMENT 
According to the World Economic Forum (“WEF”) Green Building Principles: The Action Plan for Net-Zero Carbon Buildings 
Report,  human-generated  emissions  are  largely  responsible  for  the  global  temperature  rise.  Buildings  contribute 
significantly to these emissions, accounting for 38%, with 28% stemming from day-to-day operations and 10% from 
materials and construction activities. 
KIP REIT will outline a strategy plan by achieving green building certification in future. Recognizing that green buildings 
may require higher initial investments, KIP REIT acknowledges the long-term advantages they offer. These include 
lower utility expenses due to energy-efficient designs and reduced maintenance costs, which help offset the upfront 
investments. 
Demand for green-certified buildings is strong among reputable tenants seeking environmentally responsible spaces. 
These tenants are willing to pay a premium for sustainability, which not only aligns with their environmental goals but 
also enhances their corporate reputation. The increased rental income from such tenants helps balance the initial higher 
development costs. 
KIP  REIT  remains  committed  to  its  Green  Building  initiative  in  future  by  joining  Association  that  champion  the  Green  
Building initiative in Malaysia and will continue to pursue sustainability in its property portfolio.

Our opinion

give a true and fair view of the financial position of the Group and of the Fund as at 30 June 2024, and of their financial 
performance and their cash flows for the financial year then ended in accordance with Malaysian Financial Reporting

We have audited the financial statements of the Group and of the Fund, which comprise the statements of financial 
position as at 30 June 2024 of the Group and of the Fund, and the statements of comprehensive income, statements of 
changes in net asset value and statements of cash flows of the Group and of the Fund for the financial year then ended, 
and notes to the financial statements, including material accounting policies as set out on pages 186 to 233.

We conducted our audit in accordance with approved standards on auditing in Malaysia and International Standards on

Accountants’ International Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants (including International Independence Standards) 
(“IESBA Code”), and we have fulfilled our other ethical responsibilities in accordance with the By-Laws and the IESBA 
Code.
Our audit approach
As part of designing our audit, we determined materiality and assessed the risks of material misstatement in the financial 
statements of the Group and of the Fund. In particular, we considered where the Directors made subjective judgements; 
for example, in respect of significant accounting estimates that involved making assumptions and considering future 
events that are inherently uncertain. As in all of our audits, we also addressed the risk of management override of internal 
controls, including among other matters, consideration of whether there was evidence of bias that represented a risk of 
material misstatement due to fraud.
We tailored the scope of our audit in order to perform sufficient work to enable us to provide an opinion on the financial 
statements as a whole, taking into account the structure of the Group and of the Fund, the accounting processes and 
controls, and the industry in which the Group and the Fund operate.

if, individually or in the aggregate, they could reasonably be expected to influence the economic decisions of users taken 
on the basis of these financial statements.

3 MATERIAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES
    The accounting policies set out below have been applied consistently to the period presented in these financial 
statements by KIP REIT.
(a)     Consolidation
(i) Business combination under common control
    KIP REIT applies predecessor accounting to account for business combinations under common control 
on 6 February 2017. Under the predecessor accounting, assets and liabilities acquired are not restated 
to their respective fair values but at the carrying amounts from the consolidated financial statements 
of the holding company. The difference between any consideration given and the aggregate carrying 
amounts of the assets and liabilities (at the date of the transaction) of the acquired business is recorded 
as an adjustment to retained earnings. No additional goodwill is recognised. Acquisition-related costs 
are expensed as incurred. The acquired business’ results and the related statement of financial position 
items are recognised prospectively from the date on which the business combination between entities 
under common control occurred.
(ii)     Subsidiary
    Inter-company  transactions,  balances  and  unrealised  gains  on  transactions  between  Group  and 
company are eliminated.
(ii) Investment in subsidiary
    In the Fund’s separate financial statements, investment in subsidiary is carried at cost less accumulated 
impairment losses. On disposal of investment in subsidiary, the difference between disposal proceeds 
and the carrying amount of the investment is recognised in statement of comprehensive income.
    The amount due from subsidiary of which the Fund does not expect repayment in the foreseeable future 
are considered as part of the Fund’s investment in the subsidiary.
 
(b) Investment properties
    The fair value of the investment property reflects the market conditions at the reporting date. It reflects, among 
others, rental income from current leases and reasonable and supportable assumptions that represent what 
market participants would assume about rental income from future leases in the light of current conditions. 
It also reflects, on a similar basis, any cash outflows that could be expected in respect of the property. Some 
of those outflows are reflected in liability whereas others relate to outflows that are not recognised in the 
financial statements until a later date.
    Subsequent expenditure is capitalised to the asset’s carrying amount only when it is probable that future 
economic benefits associated with the expenditure will flow to the Group and the Fund, and the cost of the 
item can be measured reliably. All other repairs and maintenance costs are expensed when incurred. When 
part of an investment property is replaced, the carrying amount of the replaced part is derecognised.
    Changes in fair values are recognised in statement of comprehensive income for the period in which it arises.
 Right-of-use assets that meet the definition of investment property
    Right-of-use assets that meet the definition of investment property in accordance with MFRS 140 is presented 
in the statement of financial position as investment property. Subsequent measurement of the right-of-use 
asset is consistent with those investment properties owned by the Group.

Equipment are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation and accumulated impairment losses.

The assessment of expected residual values and estimated useful lives of assets is carried out on an annual

    At each reporting date, the Group assesses whether there is any indication of impairment. If such indications 
exist, an analysis is performed to assess whether the carrying amount of the asset is fully recoverable. A 
write-down is made if the carrying amount exceeds the recoverable amount. Please refer to accounting policy 
on impairment of non-financial assets (Note 3(e)).
    Gains and losses on disposals are determined by comparing net disposal proceeds with carrying amount and 
are included in net property income in the statement of comprehensive income.
 
(d) Financial assets
(i)    Classification 
    The Group and the Fund have applied MFRS 9 and classify the financial assets at amortised cost.
(ii) Recognition and derecognition
    Financial assets are recognised on trade date, the date which the Group and the Fund commit to purchase 
or sell the assets. Financial assets are derecognised when the rights to receive cash flows from the 
financial assets have expired or have been transferred and the Group and the Fund have transferred 
substantially all the risks and rewards of ownership.
(iii)    Measurement
    At initial recognition, the Group and the Fund measure a financial asset at its fair value plus, in the case 
of a financial asset not at fair value through profit or loss (‘FVTPL’), transaction costs that are directly 
attributable to the acquisition of the financial asset. Transaction costs of financial assets carried at 
FVTPL are expensed in the statement of comprehensive income.
 Debt instrument
